instruction: Print the webpage to a PDF file and save it to my Desktop with the default name.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving the webpage as PDF to Desktop with default name. Evaluator verifies that the PDF file exists at the expected location and contains at least 1 page. Uses custom getter to extract PDF metadata (exists, page_count, file_size) and custom metric to verify file existence and minimum page count.
metadata.verification_details: Verified that PDF file path matches Chrome's default naming pattern for the webpage title. Minimum page count set to 1 as the webpage contains substantial content that will generate at least one PDF page without background graphics.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Instruction requires (1) print webpage to PDF, (2) save to Desktop, (3) use default name. Evaluator verifies all three: checks PDF exists at Desktop path with Chrome's default naming pattern (webpage title), and has at least 1 page

Getter logic is semantically correct: extracts PDF metadata (exists, page_count, file_size) from correct path '/home/user/Desktop/LLM Powered Autonomous Agents _ Lil'Log.pdf', which matches Chrome's default PDF naming convention for the webpage title
Metric logic is correct: properly checks file existence and minimum page count (>= 1 page), which verifies the print operation succeeded
Parameter handling for type='rule' is correct: metric directly accesses expected.get('min_pages', 1), which is correct since framework passes rules dict directly to metric function
Runtime viability confirmed: getter uses env.controller.get_file() and pypdf.PdfReader appropriately, always returns dict (never None) even on failure, proper error handling with try-except
Static validator warning about Optional vs Dict is not a runtime issue: getter implementation always returns dict with exists=False on failure, not None
